title: <weapon>.weapondef.json
description: One held object (spec 140). A weapon is a RIGID body: it does not deform, so it has no skeleton, no bind pose, no clip library and no rig family -- every one of which src/units/ exists to manage for a thing that does. What it needs instead is a grip: which point of the mesh sits in the palm, which way the business end points, and how big it should be drawn.

$comment.description: A note for whoever opens the file next. JSON has no comments and additionalProperties is false.

name.description: What a player would call it. Not the item id: an item row picks a model, and two items may pick the same one.

meshRef.description: The .glb, relative to this document. Must carry no skin and no animation -- a weapon that arrived rigged was rigged by mistake, and skinning it would cost per-vertex work for a body that moves as one piece.

socket.description: The socket it is held in when drawn, e.g. `weapon.main`. Named rather than assumed so an off-hand item is a field rather than a special case.

stowSocket.description: Where it rides when sheathed. Absent means it simply is not drawn when put away, which is the honest answer for a thing with nowhere to hang.

grip.description: How the mesh meets the hand. Every field is a measurement of THIS file rather than a convention it was asked to follow -- the next weapon will come from somewhere else.

at.description: The point in mesh coordinates that sits in the palm, before any scaling. Usually the middle of the grip.

point.description: The mesh axis running toward the business end -- the tip of a blade, the head of a hammer.

flat.description: The mesh axis normal to the flat of the blade. Fixes the roll, which `point` alone leaves free: a sword held edge-up instead of flat-up is wrong in a way nobody can describe and everybody can see. Must be perpendicular to `point`.

lengthWorld.description: How long it is drawn, tip to butt, in world units. A length rather than a scale factor, for the reason a unit's import scale is measured rather than typed: nobody can check a scale, and anybody can hold a length up against the body beside it.

provenance.description: Where the mesh came from, when that is worth recording. Free-form on purpose -- these are not paid generations with task ids to keep.
